questions.prompt: What is true about this business that no competitor can claim? Give three to six facts, separated by semicolons: the place, the people, the history, the method, a number.
questions.why: The design direction and the headline copy rest on these facts. Without them every site in the industry looks the same.

recommendation.reason: Only the owner knows these; the copy is written around the gap and never invents them.

questions.prompt: Where do visitors come from before they open the site? Pick all that apply.
questions.why: The first screen is designed for the way people arrive, for example an Instagram visitor on a phone wants the next step at once.

recommendation.reason: The usual routes for a local business.

questions.prompt: Which device do most visitors use?
questions.why: The phone is designed first when most visitors are on phones.

recommendation.reason: Most visitors to a local business use a phone.

questions.prompt: Are there legal lines the site must carry or never say? For example licence numbers, registration numbers, consent wording or disclaimers.
questions.why: Copy checks block anything that breaks these rules.

recommendation.reason: No legal line was named; the industry rules still apply.

questions.prompt: Do you have a domain name (like yourbusiness.com) and access to its settings?
questions.why: A finished site has sat unlaunched because nobody had the domain login. Asking early avoids it.

options.label: Yes, and I can change its settings
I have one but need help with it

recommendation.reason: Assumed the domain still needs sorting out.

questions.prompt: Is there a date the site must be live by?
questions.why: It decides how much is built first.
